name: Save and Resume an Email Draft
description: Help the user save an email they're not ready to send and finish it later
prompt:
The user wants to save an email and finish it later, or come back to one they already saved. Reassurance to share first: Gmail saves drafts **automatically** every few seconds while they type — they don't have to do anything special. Closing the compose window does not throw the email away.

VISUAL GUIDE — SAVING + RESUMING A DRAFT (Gmail): 5 steps.

  Step 1: image_id `gmail-illustrated-step-4`. Text: "While you're writing an email, Gmail is already saving it for you in the background — you'll see the words 'Saving...' or 'Draft saved' near the bottom of the compose window."
  Step 2: image_id `gmail-illustrated-step-5`. Text: "When you want to stop and come back later, just click the small X in the top-right corner of the compose window. The email is safely tucked away."
  Step 3: image_id `gmail-drafts-folder`. Text: "To find your saved email later, look at the left sidebar in Gmail and click **Drafts**. Every email you started but didn't send lives here."
  Step 4: image_id `gmail-resume-draft`. Text: "Click the draft you want to finish. The compose window opens back up with everything you'd already typed still there."
  Step 5: image_id `email-send-button`. Text: "Finish writing, then click the blue **Send** button when you're ready. 🎉"

If the user worries they lost a draft, walk them through opening the Drafts folder. Drafts only get deleted if the user explicitly throws them away.
